_:
PROJECT: dc2, the devcircles industry insight report. Live at https://devcircles.apexlinks.org, deployed automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds on every push to master (wait ~60-90s after a push before checking the live site). Repo root is ~/i/dc2.

GOAL OF THIS PLAN — two things, in this order:
1. DIRECT MESSAGING. An investor reading a product page can message the builder who made it, and either side can search the words of every message they have ever sent or received, across all their conversations at once. The messaging design is lifted from the sibling project ../x2 (Qdrant-stored messages keyed by a sorted conversation id) but deliberately WITHOUT x2's second Cloudflare Worker and Durable Objects: dc2 gets no ws worker, no DO, no web push, no reactions, no stickers, no folders, no mutes. Live-ness is a 5-second poll while a thread is open. That is the whole transport.
   x2 encrypts message text at rest with AES-GCM, which makes search impossible — that is exactly why dc2 does NOT copy that part. Message text is stored as plain text under the key `mx` with a Qdrant full-text payload index on it, and cross-chat search is a single `match: { text: ... }` filter. This has been verified against the live Qdrant (1.18.3): a `text` index with tokenizer `word` matches all tokens of the query (AND), and combining `must` with `should` yields `must AND (should1 OR should2 OR ...)`, which is what scopes a search to the conversations one person is in.
2. THE PRODUCT PAGE REDESIGN. /[slug] is rebuilt to a Google Stitch design: a wide hero image band, then a two-column grid — an 8-column article (overview prose, a screenshot gallery, a card list of the product's numbers, what is still unsolved, what devcircles checked) beside a 4-column sidebar (a stack of action buttons, a meta card holding tech stack / project lead / community, and a related-projects list). The Stitch mock is Material blue with Geist + Inter and a Material Symbols icon font. NONE of that palette is adopted. The user has decided: take the Stitch STRUCTURE and render it entirely in dc2's own design tokens. That is also the repo rule.

STACK: SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes only: $props $state $derived $effect $bindable — never `export let`), TypeScript, Tailwind v4, adapter-cloudflare (Workers). Package manager is pnpm, never npm or npx. Node 22 strips TypeScript types natively, so .ts test files run under `node --test` with no build step and no dependencies. Scripts: `pnpm test` (node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"), `pnpm check` (svelte-check; it exits 0 on warnings, only ERRORS fail it), `pnpm build` (vite build). NEVER start the dev server.

BASELINE BEFORE THIS PLAN: `pnpm test` = 45 passing, `pnpm check` = 0 errors / 7 warnings. If a gate shows more errors than that, the step broke something.

DATABASE: Qdrant only. One collection, `i`, shared with other projects — never create another collection, never rename it. Every row this project owns carries `s: 'adca'`. Row types live under the key `t`: `p` product, `sec` sector, `x` investor interest, and (added by this plan) `m` message and `cv` conversation. Helpers live in src/lib/server/qdrant.ts and all take `env` as their first argument, where `env` is `import { env } from '$env/dynamic/private'`.

CRITICAL QDRANT TRAP — READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY ROW. The existing `upsert()` helper attaches a 4096-dimension ZERO vector to every point under the named vector `i`. That is 16KB of RAM-resident index per row. It is fine for 43 products; it would be a disaster for messages, which are unbounded. The sibling project x2 nearly died of exactly this. Messages and conversations must therefore be written with the new `upsert_novec()` helper, which sends `vector: {}` — legal because the collection uses a NAMED vector, so a point may simply omit it at zero storage cost. Never call plain `upsert()` for a `t: 'm'` or `t: 'cv'` row.

PRODUCT PAYLOAD SCHEMA (single-letter keys, deliberate, keep it):
s tenant 'adca' | t 'p' | g slug | n name | u url | l link label (hostname) | r status: l live / p preview / u in review | c sector char | cn sector name | o one-liner | w what it does | h why it matters | x where it can grow | d launch date | q users/signups | m revenue y/n/'' | a monthly revenue naira | z team size | k proudest metric | b builder contact object {n name, e public email, p phone, l linkedin, c city, r role} | e PRIVATE ownership email, never sent to the browser | j created epoch seconds | hm headline metric value | hl headline metric label | hv v verified / s self-reported | sg stage i/b/l/r/s | ra raising y/n/'' | rt raise target text | fp founder photo url | ev evidence text | vd link last verified ISO date | hj epoch seconds the builder last confirmed figures | co country iso2 | st state slug.

NEW PRODUCT KEYS THIS PLAN ADDS (all optional strings, all default to ''):
ci cover image url (the hero band) | sc screenshots, one url per line or comma separated (the gallery) | ts tech stack, comma separated (the sidebar chips) | gh source-code url | dk documentation url. Plus `r` inside the `b` builder object: the builder's role, e.g. "principal architect".

MESSAGE ROW (t: 'm') — one per message, written with upsert_novec, id is crypto.randomUUID():
s 'adca' | t 'm' | cv conversation id | mf from email (lowercased) | mt to email (lowercased) | mx the message text, PLAIN TEXT, full-text indexed | md epoch MILLISECONDS | pg the product slug the thread is about.

CONVERSATION ROW (t: 'cv') — exactly one per pair of people, written with upsert_novec, id is `uuid_from('conv:' + cv)`:
s 'adca' | t 'cv' | cv conversation id | ma the alphabetically LOWER email | mb the higher one | pg product slug the thread started from | pn product name (denormalised so the inbox needs no second lookup) | mx preview of the last message | md epoch ms of the last message | ua unread count for ma | ub unread count for mb.
The conversation id `cv` is `[a, b].sort().join('|')` of the two lowercased emails, so both sides compute the same string and `ma` is always the lower one. That is why the unread counter is chosen by side (`ua`/`ub`) and not by name.

IDENTITY: there are no user rows. A person IS their Google email, held in the session cookie and exposed as `locals.user` = `{ e: string }` by src/hooks.server.ts. A builder is the `e` key on their product row. A signed-out visitor cannot message anyone; the sign-in link is `/google?next=/some/path` and the `next` value must match /^\/[a-z0-9\-\/]*$/ or it is ignored.

CODE STYLE, NON-NEGOTIABLE:
- snake_case for every variable and function. Payload keys, request JSON keys and page-load return keys are single letters or two letters.
- Stored enum values are single characters, mapped to words only when displayed.
- Svelte 5 runes only. Never `export let`.
- NO COMMENTS in code, except a `ponytail:` comment that names a deliberate ceiling and its upgrade path.
- No variables for single use.
- All user-facing text is lowercase — labels, buttons, headings, microcopy, everything.
- Forms submit on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter ONLY, never on a bare Enter. Use `use:ctrl_enter={fn}` from $lib/ctrl_enter on the form element. A single-input form implicitly submits on Enter in every browser, so such a form ALSO needs `onkeydown` on the input that calls `preventDefault()` when the key is Enter without ctrl/meta. Show the hint "ctrl+enter …" under the control.
- Prefer Tailwind utilities. No inline `style=` attributes anywhere, no `<style>` blocks, no raw CSS colour or size values — only the tokens defined in src/app.css.

DESIGN TOKENS (src/app.css, via Tailwind v4 @theme). Colours: `cobalt` #2b4bd7 (the one accent, links, primary buttons), `ink` #14141a (text), `paper` #faf8f4 (page background), `coral` #e85b41 (raising / danger), `ochre` #f0b429, `teal-brand` #0f8c7e (live / success), `plum` #7a3e9d. Fonts: `font-display` = Outfit (headings and numbers), `font-mono` (eyebrow labels). Opacity ramp on ink is how hierarchy is expressed: text-ink, text-ink/75, text-ink/60, text-ink/50, border-ink/10. Existing house patterns to reuse exactly: an eyebrow label is `font-mono text-xs tracking-[0.16em] text-cobalt uppercase`; a card is `rounded-lg border border-ink/10 p-6`; a tinted card is `rounded-lg bg-cobalt/5 p-6`; a primary button is `rounded-full bg-cobalt px-6 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-white hover:bg-cobalt/90`; a full-width sidebar button is the same but `rounded-lg w-full justify-center py-3`; a link is `text-cobalt hover:underline`; the underline-sweep link is `class="wipe"`. Utility classes already in app.css: `.wipe`, `.reveal`/`.shown`, `.grain`, `.tnum`.

ICONS: the Stitch mock uses the Material Symbols icon font from Google Fonts. Do not add it — no external font, no icon package. This plan creates src/lib/icon.svelte, a single inline-SVG component with a name-to-path map. Use `<Icon n="send" />`. Fonts, if any were ever needed, go in static/fonts.

IMPORT RULES THAT WILL BITE YOU:
- tsconfig sets `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions: true`, so relative imports inside src MAY carry the `.ts` extension, and files that a `node --test` test imports MUST carry it (node cannot resolve `$lib`, and cannot resolve an extensionless relative path).
- Therefore: src/lib/chat.ts imports `./filter.ts`; src/lib/detail.ts imports `./investor.ts` and `./fmt.ts`. Both of those modules must stay PURE — no `$` aliases, no npm imports, no `$env` — because their test files import them directly under plain node.
- Everything under src/lib/server/ and src/routes/ uses the `$lib/...` alias, and may import npm packages and `$env/dynamic/private`.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax` is on: a type-only import must be written `import type { X }` or `import { a, type X }`.

TESTING RULE — ABSOLUTE. Every test in this plan already exists, written by the planner, staged under plan/tests/ mirroring its destination path with a `.txt` suffix. When a step says to place one, run the exact `cp` it gives and nothing else. Do not type the test out. Do not open it to check it. Do not "fix" an import that looks wrong. Do not adapt an assertion. Make a failing test pass by changing the IMPLEMENTATION. `plan/verify_tests.sh` runs at the front of every gate and byte-compares every staged test already placed, so weakening an early test to rescue a later step fails the later step.

GIT: after each step is marked, `git add . && git commit` with a long message describing every change, then `git push`. A failed push is fine; the commit is what matters.

icon_component.s:

Create src/lib/icon.svelte with exactly this content:

<svg
	viewBox="0 0 24 24"
	fill="none"
	stroke="currentColor"
	stroke-width="1.6"

ship.s: deploy and prove the live site carries it

live_check.s:
Ship it and prove the deployed site actually carries the work, rather than trusting a green local build.

FIRST, make sure everything is committed and pushed to master. Cloudflare Workers Builds deploys automatically on push. Wait 90 seconds before checking anything.

Then run each of these against the live site and make sure every one passes. `helpa` is a real product slug that has existed since the site launched.

1. the product page renders the redesigned sections:
   curl -s https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/helpa | grep -qF 'the numbers'
   curl -s https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/helpa | grep -qF 'related projects'
   curl -s https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/helpa | grep -qF 'community'

2. the mock's placeholder copy is nowhere on the live site:
   curl -s https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/helpa | grep -qivF 'apollo analytics'

3. the private builder email is still not in the HTML. Take any owner email you can see in the local file owners.json and check the live page does not contain it. This is the one check that must never be skipped, because this step is the first time a page load reads every product row:
   curl -s https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/helpa | grep -qivF '<an email from owners.json>'

4. the messaging endpoint refuses an anonymous caller rather than writing anything:
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/api/msg -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pg":"helpa","x":"hello"}'
   must print 401.

5. the inbox refuses an anonymous visitor by sending them to sign in:
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://devcircles.apexlinks.org/inbox
   must print 302.

6. the homepage still works and still lists products:
